scope: Jamaican legal side, official sources only
method_note: FAST mode, one round. Firecrawl used for moj.gov.jm (Minister's Marriage Licence page and FAQ) and the Consulate General of Jamaica in Miami page (congenmiami.mfaft.gov.jm). mfaft.gov.jm/getting-married-in-jamaica-2/ returned 404 on 17 Nov 2026.

facts.claim: The Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs page on the Minister's Marriage Licence has a 'Residency' section that states: persons living abroad who plan to get married in Jamaica are required to be on the island at least 24 hours before the marriage ceremony; there is no restriction for persons who permanently reside on the island. It also lets parties who reside abroad use their temporary local address in Jamaica on the Form of Declaration. This shows two non-residents can apply, with a 24-hour on-island requirement rather than a residency period.
facts.publisher: Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs (Government of Jamaica)
facts.source_date: no page date shown; footer copyright 2026
facts.authority: Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs, Jamaica
facts.use_note: State it as the Ministry states it: 'on the island at least 24 hours before the ceremony'. The Consulate General in Miami (F-007) words it as 'married just 24 hours after arriving, providing prior application has been made for a marriage license'. Both agree on 24 hours. Search snippets mention a 48-hour figure on mfaft.gov.jm, but that page returned 404 and could not be verified; do not use 48 hours.

facts.claim: The Minister's Marriage Licence is granted by the Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs, giving authority to a Marriage Officer to marry a couple (single man and single woman) in Jamaica, in keeping with the Marriage Act. The Ministry FAQ states the licence only permits a marriage officer to perform the ceremony; it is not proof of marriage.
facts.publisher: Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs (Government of Jamaica)
facts.source_date: no page date shown; footer copyright 2026
facts.authority: Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs, Jamaica
facts.use_note: Second URL for the FAQ wording: https://moj.gov.jm/frequently-asked-questions-faq ('Am I legally married with the Minister's Licence? No.').

facts.claim: Procedure stated by the Ministry: obtain a blank Form of Declaration and a blank Minister's Marriage Licence form (Page 2), printed on legal size paper. A Declarant who knows there are no legal reasons preventing the marriage completes the Form of Declaration and signs it in the presence of a Justice of the Peace (JP) in Jamaica. Page 2 is left blank and taken to a Stamp Duty Office to be stamped. The completed Declaration and stamped Page 2 are returned to the Ministry with the supporting documents.
facts.publisher: Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs (Government of Jamaica)
facts.source_date: no page date shown; footer copyright 2026
facts.authority: Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs, Jamaica
facts.use_note: The FAQ says applications cannot be made online and must be lodged at the Customer Service Branch, 61 Constant Spring Road, Kingston 10, but the couple need not be present: either party, a relative or friend, the Marriage Officer, a wedding planner, hotelier or other third party may submit. Stamp Duty Offices listed in the FAQ: Kingston (72 Harbour Street), May Pen Revenue Centre, Montego Bay Revenue Centre.

facts.claim: Supporting documents for both parties, original or certified: picture identification (passport, driver's licence or Jamaica's National Identification); birth certificate; final divorce decree, decree absolute or divorce certificate (if applicable); death certificate of former spouse (if applicable); documents supporting any change of name (if applicable); letter of consent if 16 or 17 (if applicable). Where originals are presented, a set of copies is also required.
facts.publisher: Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs (Government of Jamaica)
facts.source_date: no page date shown; footer copyright 2026
facts.authority: Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs, Jamaica
facts.use_note: The FAQ adds that, without originals, copies certified by a Justice of the Peace or Notary Public may be submitted (except the Form of Declaration and blank licence form, which must be original). The Ministry does not list a separate 'proof of single status' certificate; single status is covered by the Declarant's Form of Declaration. The Consulate in Miami (F-007) asks for a birth certificate 'which includes father's name'; the Ministry does not state that.

facts.claim: All documents presented must be in English. Documents in another language should be translated by certified translators whose certification of authenticity is attached.
facts.publisher: Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs (Government of Jamaica)
facts.source_date: no page date shown; footer copyright 2026
facts.authority: Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs, Jamaica
facts.use_note: Australian documents are in English so translation is unlikely to apply. Neither the Ministry page nor FAQ mentions an Apostille or legalisation for the licence application; see the apostille fact and gaps.

facts.claim: Eligibility stated by the Ministry: both parties must be at least 18; if either party is 16 or 17, parental consent is required; neither may already be legally married to someone else. The FAQ adds the parties must not be blood relatives. The letter of consent is required from the father or guardian, signed in the presence of and certified by a JP locally or a Notary Public for an overseas party.
facts.publisher: Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs (Government of Jamaica)
facts.source_date: no page date shown; footer copyright 2026
facts.authority: Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs, Jamaica
facts.use_note: The Miami consulate page words consent as 'if under 18 years of age' without the 16 floor; follow the Ministry. Low relevance for the audience; one line is enough.

facts.claim: The Consulate General of Jamaica in Miami's official guideline for visitors states: visitors can be married 24 hours after arriving in Jamaica, provided prior application has been made for a marriage licence; no blood test is required; using a recognised marriage officer is highly recommended; notarised copies of documents are sent to the Marriage Officer and originals must be brought for the wedding; the Marriage Officer can arrange the ceremony in a church or location of your choice; ceremonies may be conducted daily between 6:00 and 20:00 EST; some hotels require documents at least 6 weeks before the date.
facts.publisher: Consulate General of Jamaica, Miami (Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade, Jamaica)
facts.use_note: Official but partly out of date: it gives the Ministry of Justice address as NCB Towers, 2 Oxford Road, Kingston 5, while the Ministry's own page gives 61 Constant Spring Road, Kingston 10. Use the Ministry address. The 6:00 to 20:00 hours and 'location of your choice' are not confirmed on moj.gov.jm or in the Marriage Act text in this round (see gaps); present them as the consulate's guidance.

facts.claim: Stamp duty for the Minister's Marriage Licence form: J$4,000.00 (Four Thousand Jamaican Dollars), paid at a Stamp Duty Office, stated by the Ministry as 'subject to change'.
facts.publisher: Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs (Government of Jamaica)
facts.source_date: no page date shown; footer copyright 2026; checked 17 Nov 2026
facts.authority: Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs, Jamaica
facts.use_note: Official fee in Jamaican dollars, not AUD. Write as 'J$4,000 stamp duty (Ministry of Justice, checked November 2026, subject to change)'. Do not convert to AUD without Nic. Marriage Officer fees are separate and set by each officer (not sourced officially).

facts.claim: Licence limits stated by the Ministry: the licence is only valid in Jamaica and expires 90 days after the date it was issued; if it expires before use, the couple must reapply. Couples are encouraged to apply at least two weeks before the wedding date; applications submitted through a hotel are processed within three weeks. Walk-in documents lodged by 12:00 noon Monday to Thursday, or 11 a.m. Friday, may be processed the same day or next business day.
facts.publisher: Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs (Government of Jamaica)
facts.source_date: no page date shown; footer copyright 2026
facts.authority: Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs, Jamaica
facts.use_note: Good for the timeline section: book the ceremony date, then apply within the 90-day window and at least two weeks ahead (three weeks if the resort applies).

facts.claim: The Ministry FAQ states that a ceremony under the Minister's Licence may be performed by 'an appointed Marriage Officer or any person appointed by the Minister to do so'. The Consulate General in Miami recommends using a recognised marriage officer and points to visitjamaica.com for a listing of recognised marriage officers.
facts.publisher: Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs (Government of Jamaica)
facts.authority: Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs, Jamaica; Consulate General of Jamaica, Miami (https://congenmiami.mfaft.gov.jm/marriage_jamaica)
facts.use_note: Do not say a friend can officiate. The visitjamaica.com marriage officer listing was not opened in this round.

facts.claim: Jamaica Information Service: after the wedding, the marriage register must be submitted to the Registrar General's Department for the marriage certificate to be processed, produced and printed. Five signatures must be on the marriage register to make the marriage valid: the couple, the 2 witnesses and the marriage officer.
facts.source_date: no date shown on the programme page
facts.authority: Jamaica Information Service; Registrar General's Department named as registering body
facts.use_note: This is the official source for 'two witnesses'. Minimum witness age and whether witnesses need ID were not found on an official page (see gaps). Do not state an age.

facts.claim: Ministry FAQ: the Minister's Licence does not make you legally married; after the ceremony the couple must apply for the Marriage Certificate (legal proof of marriage) from the Registrar General's Department (rgd.gov.jm). The Consulate General in Miami states that the copy of the Marriage Register given after the ceremony, signed by the Marriage Officer, couple and witnesses, 'is NOT a legal document'; the certified copy of the marriage certificate may be applied for by the Marriage Officer, takes 7 working days to 1 month, and express service is available.
facts.publisher: Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs (Government of Jamaica)
facts.authority: Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs, Jamaica; Consulate General of Jamaica, Miami (https://congenmiami.mfaft.gov.jm/marriage_jamaica); issuing body is the Registrar General's Department
facts.use_note: Processing time comes from the consulate only; rgd.gov.jm was not reached in this round, so the RGD's own current timing and fee are unconfirmed (see gaps). Key reader message: leave Jamaica with a plan for the RGD certified copy, not just the register copy.

facts.claim: Ministry FAQ: Jamaica's Marriage Certificate is widely accepted in other territories, but it is the responsibility of foreigners marrying on the island to ensure the Jamaican Marriage Certificate is recognised in their homeland before the ceremony.
facts.publisher: Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs (Government of Jamaica)
facts.authority: Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs, Jamaica
facts.use_note: Pair with an Australian source on recognition of overseas marriages (ag.gov.au or smartraveller.gov.au) in batch B; not researched here.

facts.claim: The HCCH status table for the Apostille Convention (5 October 1961) lists Jamaica as a contracting party by accession, with entry into force on 3 July 2021, and Australia by accession, in force 16 March 1995. A Jamaican public document such as an RGD marriage certificate can therefore be authenticated for use in Australia by Apostille rather than consular legalisation.
facts.publisher: Hague Conference on Private International Law (HCCH)
facts.source_date: status table as at 30 June 2026 per page summary
facts.use_note: The second sentence is an inference from treaty status, not a statement by a Jamaican or Australian authority. Which Jamaican office issues Apostilles, the fee, and whether Australian authorities require one for a Jamaican certificate were not confirmed (see gaps). The Miami consulate only says 'your country may require the certificate to be legalized; contact your Embassy or Consulate'. Neither the Ministry page nor FAQ asks for Apostilled Australian documents for the licence.

facts.claim: Same-sex marriage is not available in Jamaica. Section 18(2) of the Constitution of Jamaica (Charter of Fundamental Rights and Freedoms) states: 'No form of marriage or other relationship referred to in subsection (1), other than the voluntary union of one man and one woman may be contracted or legally recognized in Jamaica.' The Ministry of Justice describes the Minister's Marriage Licence as authority to marry 'a couple (single man and single woman)', and its FAQ limits eligibility to 'a man and woman'.
facts.publisher: Constitute Project (text of the Constitution of Jamaica 1962, as amended to 2023); confirmed by Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs, https://moj.gov.jm/node/119
facts.authority: Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs, Jamaica (licence eligibility); constitutional text via Constitute Project
facts.use_note: Cite moj.gov.jm/node/119 as the outbound link (official). The constitutional quote is from a reputable compilation, not an official Jamaican government copy; an official consolidated text was not reached (laws.moj.gov.jm under maintenance). Some commentary cites 18(1) rather than 18(2); quote 18(2) as above. Keep tone factual.

Re-check the Act when the portal is back or via the Legal Information Portal of Jamaica.
